Include UIF 4 in five minutes

Development build: use the essential runtime for modal, dropdown, tabs, accordion, collapse and toast. No chart, editor, full icon catalog or AI authoring server is downloaded. Copy dist/v4/essential.js and essential.css to your assets directory, then use an external bootstrap:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/uif/v4/essential.css">
<script type="module" src="/assets/app-bootstrap.js"></script>

// app-bootstrap.js
import { startEssential } from '/assets/uif/v4/essential.js';
const application = startEssential(document);
// After an application-owned partial update:
// application.refresh(changedSubtree);
// On application teardown:
// application.destroy();

Importing alone does not mount controls. Do not start the broad compatibility runtime on the same subtree. Open the generated canonical example. dist/v4/manifest.json records measured JS/CSS bytes and SRI; application bootstrap, data and assets are additional.

Selected profiles: web controls, RAD CRUD integration, mobile shell, desktop workspace. Include exactly one profile JS/CSS pair; use the full bundle's selected starters for staged legacy adoption. See the entry-point and ownership contract. Static JSON demonstrates RAD response handling, not a production backend.

Theme author journey

A single typed JSON pack builds responsive web, mobile bottom navigation and desktop workspace previews, with scoped light/dark tokens. These are browser layouts, not native OS applications. Token contrast checks supplement rendered and manual accessibility checks.

npm run theme -- create brand.json brand
npm run theme -- validate brand.json
npm run theme -- build brand.json output/brand

Compiler, token subset, CLI and trust boundaries · Theme schema · Web preview · Mobile preview · Desktop preview

AI authoring journey

Give Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant the compact context, schema and starter pack. Validate its returned JSON locally using the same CLI. Local MCP discovery/build/export tools are optional; no model SDK or provider credential enters the browser runtime. Hosted connector acceptance and public OAuth deployment are not yet verified.

Simple JS/CSS Distribution

Build output includes plain browser files for apps that do not use TypeScript or a bundler: dist/uif.css, dist/uif.esm.js, and dist/uif.iife.js.

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/uif/uif.css">
<script src="/assets/uif/uif.iife.js"></script>
<script>BatoiUIF.autoStart();</script>

Core Concepts

import { init } from '@batoi/uif-core';
init(document);

Data Attributes

Use data-uif, data-uif-action, data-uif-target, data-uif-src, data-uif-swap, and package-specific attributes to enhance server-rendered HTML.

CSS Tokens

The generated design-token reference is published with light, dark, compact, high-contrast, forced-colors, and reduced-motion modes.

:root {
  --uif-color-primary: #2563eb;
  --uif-space-4: 1rem;
}

Components

Component coverage includes modal, drawer, dropdown, tabs, toast, accordion, alert, badge, breadcrumb, collapse, tooltip, popover, progress, spinner, skeleton, pagination, command menu, navbar/sidebar, stepper/wizard, file upload, and combobox. The component gallery also demonstrates professional app-pattern primitives such as button matrices, toolbars, form sections, metric rows, hero banners, summary blocks, inspectors, stat cards, empty states, filter builders, notification panels, and picker wrappers.

Components initialize from declarative markup and include ARIA defaults.
data-uif="dropdown" closes on outside click and Escape.

App Primitives

Production app layouts can use fixed shells, sidebar nav, page heads, scroll regions, stat cards, kanban boards, queue rows, timelines, risk bands, semantic badges, density modes, and accent switching.

<html data-uif-density="compact">
<main class="uif-app-shell-fixed">
  <aside class="uif-sidebar"><nav class="uif-sidebar-nav">...</nav></aside>
  <section class="uif-shell-content">
    <header class="uif-page-head">...</header>
    <div class="uif-scroll-region">...</div>
  </section>
</main>

Charts

Charts are dependency-free SVG and support line, area, bar, horizontal bar, grouped bar, stacked bar, pie, donut/doughnut, radar, sparkline, metric, progress/ring, gauge, timeline, heatmap, bullet, and statistical charts such as histogram, box plot, scatter, regression, control chart, distribution, and Pareto.

<div data-uif="chart" data-uif-chart="radar"
  data-uif-data='[{"label":"Security","value":82},{"label":"Performance","value":74}]'></div>

AI UI

MCP Tool Approval

Attribute Registry

UIF standardizes attributes such as data-uif, data-uif-action, data-uif-target, data-uif-src, data-uif-state, data-uif-model, data-uif-options, and data-uif-persist. Canonical component and envelope references are generated from typed source during every build.

<button data-uif-action="toggle" data-uif-target="#drawer">Toggle</button>

Security Model

Dynamic text in forms, realtime feeds, AI UI, MCP UI, and generated table rows is rendered as text by default. Server-rendered partial swaps remain supported for RAD workflows and are treated as trusted backend HTML.

import { setText, setTrustedHTML, swapTrustedHTML } from '@batoi/uif-dom';

setText(el, userControlledValue);
setTrustedHTML(el, serverRenderedHtml, { trusted: true });
swapTrustedHTML(target, serverRenderedPartial, 'inner');

Browser-side AI and MCP packages are UI-only. Database access, file writes, email, payments, deployments, MCP invocation, permissions, and audit logging must remain server-side.

Roadmap

UIF 4 development focuses on selective imports, smaller includes, typed themes, provider-neutral authoring and stronger accessibility/lifecycle evidence. The broad 3.1 compatibility facade remains available during adoption; GA requires the published release gates and actual integration acceptance.
